art.zoomFit: Fit the sheet to the panel
art.renumberMessage: Changing the width renumbers every sprite. Your map tiles and the calls in your code are rewritten to match.
art.renumberCalls: {{n}} calls in your code are rewritten.
art.renumberUnsure: {{n}} calls name a sprite with something other than a plain number, so nothing can follow those — check them yourself.
art.shrinkMessage: {{n}} drawn sprites fall outside a sheet that size. They stay in the file and come back if you grow it again, but nothing can reach them meanwhile.
art.flagsHelp:
Eight bits per sprite. The engine ignores them; your game reads them with `map.flag(index, bit)`.

What each bit means is yours to decide: flag 0 can mean solid, flag 2 water.
art.pickSprite: Sheet map — drag to pick the cells you are working on
art.deleteSheetMessage:
Its art goes with it.

The sprite numbers after it shift down, so code that names one of them will point at the next sprite along.

map.sizeNote: Tiles keep their place, so nothing is renumbered and no code is rewritten.
map.shrinkMessage: {{n}} placed tiles fall outside a map that size. They stay in the file and come back if you grow it again, but nothing can reach them meanwhile.
map.gridHelp:
Fine grid every tile, sky rule every eight.

The screen is 40×22½ tiles.
map.flagsHelp:
Tints each tile by the first flag set on its sprite.

Flags are per sprite, not per tile.
map.deleteMapMessage:
Its tiles go with it.

Code that draws it by number will draw the next map along, or nothing.

editor.viewerPoppedHint: The game keeps running in the floating panel and follows you across editors.

sound.removeInstrumentMessage:
Its notes go from {{patterns}} pattern(s), and {{sfx}} sound effect slot(s) fall silent.

Undo brings it all back.
sound.sfxHelp:
Numbered slots your game plays with `sound.play_sfx(slot)`.

Click a slot to put the current pattern in it. Click it again to clear it.

A free row always waits at the end, so there is always another number.
sound.clearMessage:
This empties the pattern of its {{n}} notes.

Anything that plays it, a music or a sound effect, keeps its place and falls silent.
sound.emptyHint: An instrument is a wave plus an envelope. Add one and the piano roll wakes up — five voices, sixteen slots.
sound.noInstrument: The inspector fills in once an instrument exists.
sound.name: Instrument name
sound.oscHelp:
The raw wave.

Square has a `duty` cycle. Noise ignores pitch. `PCM` plays a sample you bring.
sound.presetsLead: Click a sound to hear it. The name is the instrument's.
sound.envHelp:
How loud the note is over its life.

`Attack` is the rise, `decay` the fall to the `sustain` level, `release` the fade once the note ends.
sound.modHelp:
Vibrato wobbles the pitch.

Arp walks a chord with one voice: write several notes on one step.

The filter shapes the tone, keeping the lows, the highs or a band between.
sound.mixHelp:
Per-instrument level and stereo position.

Every note this instrument plays goes through them.
sound.unused: Not used yet — paint some notes.
sound.sampleHint: Any audio file. Mixed to mono and resampled to 8-bit / 8 kHz — {{seconds}} s fits the budget.
sound.zoomReset: Back to one step per cell
sound.shortenMessage: {{n}} note(s) past the new end will go. Undo brings them back.
sound.musicHelp:
A music is a grid of pattern numbers, played left to right, then top to bottom.

Each pattern keeps its own tempo and length, so a chain can change speed halfway. An empty box with music after it is a hole, drawn in orange: playing stops before it.

The game starts one with `sound.play_music(0)`.
sound.newInstrumentLead: Start from a sound, or from a blank square wave.
sound.fromPresetHint: Pick a sound to start from. Every dial stays yours to change.
sound.customHint: A plain square wave with a short envelope, to set up yourself.
sound.sampleTrimmed: Trimmed to the first {{seconds}} s — that is the whole budget.

net.helpState:
Every path the game declares, and, while a session runs, what it holds.

`R` and `W` say whether joined clients may read or write a path. The host is never restricted.
net.noSession: Set a path up here before you run anything, and the flags travel with the game. The values fill in when it calls net.host() or net.join().
net.whoHelp:
Everyone in this work session can take a player slot.

Anyone else needs the code.
net.playersHelp:
The game declared its player count with `net.host()`.

Slots fill as peers connect.
net.testHelp:
Spawns a second client on this machine that joins your session, so you can test netplay alone.

Latency and loss are applied to that client's outgoing frames, not to yours.
net.rigWaiting: Waiting for this client to call net.join().
net.deleteNode: Delete this node and its children
net.hostOnly: Only the host can change the shape of a path a session is holding.
net.needHost: Host a session first — run the game and call net.host().
net.relayOnlyHelp: Refuses the direct path, to measure what a relayed session costs. Real traffic through the provider, so it spends the allowance. Applies to the next session.

consent.title: Usage analytics
consent.body: May Naucto measure how the site is used, to make it better? It keeps a first-party cookie and shares nothing with anyone else. Refusing changes nothing else on the site.
consent.learnMore: What is measured, and for how long
consent.choiceHint: Measure how you use Naucto under a first-party cookie. You can change this at any time.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: Naucto measures how it is used to see what to improve. It never sells or shares this data, shows no advertising, and runs no third-party trackers. You decide below whether your visits are measured.

accepted.pages: The pages you open, by name (a game page, not which game), and how long your visits last, under a random id kept in a cookie for 13 months and a visit id kept 30 minutes.
accepted.plays: The games you play and how long they run, and the time you spend in the editor.
accepted.context: Your device type, browser and system family, country, screen size range and language, and the site or campaign that brought you. Your address is only used to find the country and is never kept.
accepted.account: When you are signed in, these visits are linked to your account, so you can see your own play time in Settings.

privacy.refusedTitle: If you refuse, or do not answer

refused.nothingStored: Nothing is stored on your device, apart from your choice once you make it.
refused.ping: While a tab is visible, it tells us about once a minute whether a game is running, with no id of any kind, so we know how many people are on Naucto.
refused.plays: Games started and how long they run are counted per game, with no id of any kind.
refused.views: A game’s public play count still goes up when you press Play, with nothing that identifies you.

retention.raw: Visits, page views and plays: 90 days.
retention.aggregate: Totals per day, week and month, with no id of any kind: kept.
retention.history: Your own play history by day, when you are signed in: while your account exists.
retention.choice: Your choice: six months, then you are asked again.

privacy.rights: Signed in, you can see what was counted for your account, download it, or erase it, in Settings. Deleting your account erases it too.
privacy.geoCredit: Country lookups use IP geolocation by
